public_rationale: On a plain reading, the claim is that leading generative models still failed in substantial, reproducible ways on reasoning and visual tasks. Nguyen's group's paper (v3, November 2025) found GPT-5 and Grok-4 still badly biased on simple counting, with GPT-5 at about 31%. In February 2026, a 53-model test found 42 models gave the wrong answer to a one-step car-wash reasoning question. There is real counterevidence: Google reported a 77.1% ARC-AGI-2 score for Gemini 3.1 Pro, a big reasoning gain. But that gain does not show the documented failures had gone. On balance, the evidence supports the claim as worded.
limitations: 'Serious' is a judgment, and a reviewer weighing benchmark gains more heavily might call this mixed.
The visual study did not test the very newest models available at the post date.
The car-wash test was run by a commercial vendor.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, leading generative AI models, including vision-language models, still showed substantial and reproducible failures on reasoning and visual tasks that are easy for humans.
Progress on some benchmarks does not falsify the claim. Absence of documented serious failures would.
Target period: from 2025-09-01 to the post date (2026-03-01). This is the recent period that public evaluations of then-current models could report on.
criteria.support_condition: Published evaluations from the period show current frontier models failing badly on simple reasoning or visual tasks, such as counting or obvious one-step inferences.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations from the period show frontier models reliably solving such tasks, with the failures Marcus cites gone in then-current models.

evidence.excerpt: However, GPT-5 still falls far short of expectations, and these latest results do not change our conclusions that VLMs remain biased toward canonical answers on our VLMBias.
evidence.publisher: arXiv (Vo, Nguyen, Taesiri, Dang, Nguyen, Kim)
evidence.explanation: A then-recent frontier model (GPT-5) still failed badly at simple visual counting of familiar subjects. This supports the visual-cognition part.

evidence.excerpt: We also observe similarly poor and biased behaviors in the most recently released models of GPT-5 (OpenAI, 2025a) and Grok-4 (xAI, 2025)
evidence.publisher: arXiv (Vo, Nguyen, Taesiri, Dang, Nguyen, Kim)
evidence.explanation: The failures held across the newest models tested, not only older ones.

evidence.excerpt: On a single call, only 11 out of 53 models got it right. 42 said walk.
evidence.explanation: Most current models failed a one-step reasoning prompt in February 2026. This supports the reasoning part. Opper sells an AI gateway, so its framing deserves some caution.

evidence.excerpt: Google says Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved a verified score of 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2 and calls that “more than double” the reasoning performance of Gemini 3 Pro.
evidence.locator: section 'Google highlights an ARC-AGI-2 “verified” score of 77.1%'
evidence.explanation: Shows strong and fast-improving reasoning on a hard novel-pattern benchmark. This cuts against calling reasoning problems 'serious', though it does not show the documented failures were gone.
